title: Dossier catalog: create a product dossier
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar reading "ANDS Studio" with the sub-label "dossier manager", plus a user chip and links: "Help", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", and "Guided journey →". The main heading is "Your product dossiers", with a paragraph explaining that a Dossier ID "is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada" and that workspaces are isolated per client. While data loads you see "Loading dossiers…"; if you have none, a notice says "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission."

To the right of the heading is a "New dossier +" button (it toggles to "Cancel"). Clicking it opens an inline card with two fields: "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). Small print explains: "Health Canada issues your Dossier ID when you file a Dossier ID Request through REP (via your CESG account)." If you don't have one, a small link — "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →" — auto-fills a draft ID starting with "d" plus six random digits. You must know the ID format: entering anything other than one letter plus 6–7 digits shows the error "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)".

You click "Create & open →" (it reads "Creating…" while busy) and are taken straight into the dossier's Module 1 workspace: a three-column layout with a section tree on the left, a section editing panel in the middle, and a right rail showing a submission tower, a module progress bar with "required sections complete" counts, and three readiness flags — "Documents", "Fee", and "Valid eCTD".

Back on the catalog, each dossier is a clickable tile showing its ID, product title, submission type with "CS-BE", a progress bar, and a status chip: either "Ready to file" or a count like "3/5 modules". Placeholder dossiers carry a badge "draft ID — set real ✎"; clicking it opens a browser prompt: "Enter the Dossier ID issued by Health Canada (one letter + 6–7 digits, e.g. e123456). All documents, sequences and history move with it." Each tile also has an "✕" delete button; clicking it triggers a browser confirmation: "Delete dossier {id} and all of its documents? This cannot be undone." Both the rename prompt and delete confirmation use native browser dialogs, not styled modals. Any API error appears as a red notice banner on the page.
